title: Completed stalk comparisons and source reparametrization
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $Z\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{f}X$ be morphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete integral constructible categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], their raw rationalizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the completed pullbacks of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Specify their composition comparisons by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ or $E$, any one of these schemes $T$, a geometric point $v:s\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $M\in D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$, put $J_v(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(Lv^*M)$, with [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. In the comparison for $f$ below take $v:s\to Y$ and $M\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$; in the reparametrization comparison take $M$ on the target of $v$.

There are natural $\Lambda$-linear comparison isomorphisms
$$c_{f,v,M}:J_v(Lf^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{fv}(M),\qquad r_{v,\alpha,M}:J_v(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{v\delta}(M),\quad\delta=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),\quad\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(k).$$
Here $c$ uses the specified pullback-composition comparison, and $r$ is normalized by the finite-level germ rule $[U,u,a]\mapsto[U,u\delta,a]$ in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Their integral constructions realize these comparisons as maps of the simultaneous strict reduction diagrams, using the comparisons of [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence]; their rational constructions are their images under rationalization. In particular, the asserted equalities are equalities of those specified maps, not merely equality of their individual reductions.

For $w:s\to Z$, write $\chi_{h,f}:L(fh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lf^*$. Then
$$c_{fh,w,M}=c_{f,hw,M}\circ c_{h,w,Lf^*M}\circ J_w(\chi_{h,f,M}),\qquad c_{\mathrm{id},v,M}=1,$$
$$r_{fv,\alpha,M}\circ c_{f,v,M}=c_{f,v\delta,M}\circ r_{v,\alpha,Lf^*M}.$$
If $\epsilon=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta)$, then $r_{v\delta,\beta,M}\circ r_{v,\alpha,M}=r_{v,\beta\circ\alpha,M}$, and $r_{v,1,M}=1$; equivalently the composite reparametrizes by $\delta\circ\epsilon$. All these comparisons are natural in arbitrary morphisms of the specified integral or rational categories.

For $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ and any such $\delta$, let $j_{\delta,N}:\operatorname{Fib}_sN\to\operatorname{Fib}_sL\delta^*N$ be restriction of sections along $\delta$, followed by inverse-image colimit insertion and the inverse-image/pullback comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (and rationalization for $E$). Under the identity-point identification $J_{\mathrm{id}}(N)=\operatorname{Fib}_sN$, one has
$$c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}\circ j_{\delta,N}=r_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,N}.$$
This last equation is compatible with any finite succession of source automorphisms and with the comparisons for $v:s\to X$. No Weil structure, periodic point, or endomorphism of $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: For the local pointUnits obligation, the finite-field cardinality gives characteristic p on the base field and then on its algebraic closure. The distinct prime l is a unit in k; map it through global sections into each stalk and then into each residue field. For sectionsRoos_existsUnique, use the proved point-sections product comparison and the normalized Roos isomorphism of lem-trf-point-quotient-augmentation-diagram. Both coordinate identities are its coordinate equations. Convert the degreewise equations to the whole-map equations of scalarRoosMap_existsUnique in lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension; its uniqueness implies equality of the underlying chain maps, hence of the isomorphisms.

For sectionRestriction_existsUnique use the proved scalar_normalization calculation in the module of lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural. This calculation has no prime-to-characteristic hypothesis: finite constant sections are unchanged by the coefficient transport, and the completed identity follows by its finite projections. Apply the inverse coefficient map to obtain the scalar identity for restriction along the source automorphism. Module restriction is therefore linear for the transported action. Presheaf naturality makes these linear maps a natural transformation. The sourceArrow is the hom of the site isomorphism induced by sourceIso; the underlying restriction is consequently bijective. The forgetful functor on modules reflects isomorphisms, so the transformation is a natural isomorphism. Its formula on every section proves uniqueness by extensionality.

Work first over $R=\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-trf-bounded-quotient-stalk-realization], choose the simultaneous quotient tower and its bounded zigzag and identify $J_v(M)$ with $H(((P_n)_v)_n)$ on both cone coordinates. Use [lem-trf-stalk-compositor-tower-realization] to define $c=\Gamma(s,\chi^{-1})$ in these coordinates, and [lem-trf-germ-reparametrization-derived-descent] to define $r$ by the germ tower map. These are natural $R$-linear isomorphisms for arbitrary integral derived morphisms, independent of representatives.

proof.text: Realize the strict composition, unit and mixed tower equations of [lem-trf-stalk-compositor-tower-realization]. Its identification of the last factor with $J_w(\chi_{h,f,M})$ gives exactly the asserted formula for $c_{fh,w,M}$, the identity formula and the mixed formula. The action and unit equations of [lem-trf-germ-reparametrization-derived-descent] give the asserted $r$ equations with the order $\beta\circ\alpha$. These equalities concern specified whole-tower maps.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, input (b); assembly step 2 from extracted strict-tower lemmas

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-source-section-stalk-cone-comparison] to $N$: its chain-map equality is $e_\delta c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}j_{\delta,N}\Gamma(q)=H(R_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,\bullet})e_{\mathrm{id}}\Gamma(q)$. Exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] make $\Gamma(q)$ invertible after localization. Cancel it and $e_\delta$, and substitute the definition of $r$ from [lem-trf-germ-reparametrization-derived-descent]. This proves the section equation.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, input (b); assembly step 3 from extracted strict-tower lemmas

proof.text: For compatibility at $v$ apply the section equation to $N=Lv^*M$, whose constructibility follows from [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1). At each appended source automorphism substitute $c_{\delta,\mathrm{id}}j_\delta=r$, pass $r$ through $c$ by the mixed equation of Step 2, and combine adjacent $r$'s by its action law. Induction starting with the identity gives every finite succession and its compatibility with the comparisons for $v$.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, input (b); assembly step 4 from extracted strict-tower lemmas

proof.text: For $E$ use [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: objects keep integral representatives, and $f\otimes a$ acts on fibres by $a(\Gamma(s,f)\otimes E)$. Apply this functor to the integral comparisons, inverses and equations. Naturality for a simple tensor follows from integral naturality and $R$-linearity, and for every rational morphism by additivity over a finite sum of simple tensors. This proves all rational assertions without an integrality hypothesis on morphisms.
